grand_strategy.reading: Ireland is a small EU member outside NATO, with a neutral military tradition, a Partnership for Peace relationship, and an economy built on US multinationals. Its strategy uses the EU as its anchor and the 2026 Council presidency as its lever, keeps the UK relationship stable through the Northern Ireland framework, and takes a visible line on Gaza that has cost it an embassy relationship with Israel. Its thin defence means the Russia question is handled mainly through EU sanctions and partner monitoring of undersea cables.

stances.note: Closest neighbour, mirrored from the GBR card (its IRL row, same links). Partner by structure: shared border, Common Travel Area, Good Friday Agreement, Windsor Framework. Open items: the SPS text, still unsigned in Oct 2026, and the legacy legislation. Bond - kin: shared history and Northern Ireland.

stances.note: No source calls Russia a rival: this is our reading of the structure (confidence C). Ireland applies EU sanctions and backs Ukraine (21st package, July 2026; the Aughinish Alumina plant, owned by Russia's Rusal, exported about 45% of 2025 sales to Russia and the government would not list it yet). Russia is a maritime and cable threat: a 2022 naval live-fire exercise 250 km off Cork was moved outside Irish waters after protest, and a Russia-bound cargo ship dragged its anchor near subsea cables off Mayo in 2025. Russia is not a mortal enemy: Dublin keeps an embassy in Moscow. Bond - none: no kinship, no grievance.

The Occupied Territories Bill became law on 23 July 2026, banning imports of settlement goods (services excluded). Israel recalled its ambassador in 2024 and on 15 Dec 2024 announced closing its Dublin embassy, citing recognition and Ireland's ICJ intervention; Dublin called the charges 'outright false'. Trade and EU relations continue (necessity), while Ireland resists alignment with Israel on Gaza: reluctant partner. Grade is our reading (confidence C); not a mortal enemy - no aim to destroy Israel. Bond - none.
